Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $35 million class fund distributed automatically to identified members. Brightline would separately pay up to $3 million in court-approved fees and expenses; any amount not awarded would instead benefit the class. We are ready to discuss the fund amount, but automatic distribution is important given Brightline's records.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree automatic payments are appropriate given the available records. We can offer a $30 million class fund plus up to $2.5 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with any unawarded fees benefiting the class. We would retain the right to address the fee request before the court.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline's latest term sheet: a $30 million class fund distributed automatically, plus up to $2.5 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with no clear-sailing provision and any unawarded fees benefiting the class. We will work with you to document the agreement for court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial class recovery and automatic distribution, since Brightline can identify every member and charged card. Keep fees separate from class relief, with any unawarded fees going to the class. The firm's fixed compensation does not depend on settlement fees.

The opening proposal is within authority and has court-friendly distribution and fee terms, but there is room to negotiate a lower total outlay. Preserve automatic distribution and avoid fee provisions that could undermine approval.

The $30 million automatic-distribution fund exceeds the $27.5 million trial-value estimate before accounting for certification risk, delay, and litigation costs. The fee terms avoid a clear-sailing agreement and return any unawarded fees to the class. Acceptance is in the class's interest.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: Hargrove Lane LLP negotiated directly with Brightline’s counsel. Class relief and attorneys’ fees were addressed during the same negotiation; we do not represent that fees were discussed only after class relief was agreed. The resulting agreement provides a $30 million class fund, with payments made automatically to identifiable class members, and up to $2.5 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses. Brightline retains the right to oppose the fee request, and any fees not awarded will benefit the class rather than revert to Brightline. The agreement remains subject to court approval.
